decisions.executionNote: Approach the two white support blocks in separate workspaces with open grippers; gradually pitch wrists down while retaining elbow-up continuity.
Fine approach to rear-left and front-right supports; lower slowly and align each wrist with its block, using wrist views to refine before closing.
Center both blocks between the fingers using wrist image offsets, close fully, and make a short test lift to check retention.
Lift the retained supports clear of the table, then carry them inward to a symmetric base pair while straightening their yaw. Keep both grippers closed.
Seat both supports gently at table height, open, and lift away. Check base alignment before handling the lower board.
Withdraw vertically from the released supports, spread to board-end approach positions, and gradually turn both grippers inward for a level two-arm board grasp.
Complete the inward-facing board-grasp orientations above the table, moving outside each end with both grippers open.
Lower and converge symmetrically onto the ends of the long board, then close both grippers; verify a level grasp before transport.
Lift the long board level with both grippers closed, then carry it above the two upright base supports, keeping symmetric arm motion.
Lower the long board onto the base pair, pause to seat it, release both grippers, and begin withdrawing without disturbing the supports.
Clear the stable lower board and approach the remaining left and right white blocks from above, gradually reorienting for upright support grasps.
Finish turning to the upright-block grasp orientation while descending above each remaining white support. Leave a small height margin to refine the wrist-view centering.
Refine centering and yaw from the wrist views, descend to the block grasp height, close fully, and make a short test lift before transporting the middle supports.
Lift the white supports clear of the lower board, then carry them inward while straightening their yaw. Keep both grippers closed and check their retention visually.
Center the two retained middle supports over the lower board at symmetric left/right positions, compensating for their grasp offsets, then lower toward seating height.
Seat the middle supports with a slow final descent, release both grippers, then lift clear for a visual check of uprightness and alignment.
Move clear of the newly released supports toward the shorter board, spreading the arms and turning the grippers inward. Keep open and avoid brushing the tower.
The lower layer and both middle supports appear upright. Finish aligning the opposing grippers above the shorter board and lower to a pre-grasp height.
Converge and descend symmetrically onto the short board ends, then close both grippers fully while holding the board level.
Keep both grippers closed, lift the short board level above the middle supports, and begin transporting toward the tower.
Carry the retained short board above the middle supports, gently equalizing the end heights before seating it. Keep both grippers fully closed.
Seat the middle board slowly onto both upright supports, release symmetrically, then lift away slightly to inspect stability and centering.
Withdraw clear of the seated middle board. Move each arm toward its own remaining top piece, turning gradually while maintaining height and open grippers.
Approach the green cap and small wooden top board from above in separate workspaces, completing steeper pitched grasp orientations. Refine from the next wrist views before closing.
Use wrist-image offsets to center the cap and small board, lower toward their grasp heights, and align the right gripper with the board's long axis. Pause open for a visual check.
Close on the centered top pieces and lift vertically for a retention check. Keep the cap outside the tower while preparing to place the small board first.
The right board remains in the gripper, but the green cap stayed on the table. Raise and turn the board toward the tower; reopen and lower the left gripper for a deeper cap grasp.
Regrasp the cap slightly above the table-contact height and test lift. Carry the small board toward the tower center while completing its horizontal alignment, keeping the right gripper closed.
Center and seat the small top board, then release it. The cap was not retained; reopen and change to a side-on grasp approach rather than repeating the missed grasp.
Withdraw the right arm from the released top board. Complete the left side-facing cap approach and lower slowly, keeping open for a final alignment check.
Align the side-facing left gripper with the cap, close and test-lift. Move the empty right arm clear of the tower toward its home workspace, rotating gradually.
The side grasp appears to retain the cap. Lift it well above tower height and straighten its yaw before inward transport; continue returning the empty right arm toward home.
Carry the retained cap above the top board at clearance height, staying in the left workspace. Bring the empty right arm close to its original pose with gradual rotation.
Center the retained cap over the small board using the observed lateral offset and lower cautiously toward seating height. Finish the right arm's return to its initial pose.
Make a small centering correction and gently seat the cap on the top board, then open the left gripper and lift clear to inspect the completed stack.
The cap remains on its board after release. Lift clear, then withdraw the left arm toward its origin with gradual orientation change, leaving both grippers open.
The full stack appears stable and upright. Continue the left arm's gradual return to origin, staying clear of the tower with both grippers open.
Finish returning the left arm to its original pose with a tapered motion and both grippers open; maintain clearance from the stable tower.
